thread:
Alex: CI red on windows-container-build (job windows-build/win-latest). Build failed then push returned 403. Root error in logs: 'ln: Operation not permitted' while committing a layer. Anyone seen this after a Dockerfile change?
Jen: Which PR touched the Dockerfile?
Alex: PR #6421 https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/6421 — added a RUN that creates symlinks inside the windows base stage and adjusted COPY --from=builder /app /app.
Ravi: Can you rerun the job? Sometimes transient.
Alex: Reran twice, same result.
CI-Bot: build log excerpt:
```
# error
ln: failed to create symbolic link '/app/tools/link': Operation not permitted
error building image: failed to commit layer: "symlink target not allowed"
remote: error: upload failed with status 403
```
Melissa: sounds like NTFS vs Linux layer semantics. We build on Linux hosts with buildx but the base image is windows servercore — creating symlinks in that context can produce invalid layer metadata. Did the author test on Windows? :thinking:
Alex: author tested locally on Linux using docker buildx; they didn't run a Windows container locally.
Jen: Quick mitigation: revert the symlink creation in the Dockerfile and create the symlink at container startup in entrypoint (shell script or powershell). Less risky.
Rohit: Or build the image with platform windows/amd64 and run the symlink command using PowerShell syntax: `SHELL [\"powershell\", \"-Command\"]` + `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path \"C:\\app\\tools\\link\" -Target \"C:\\app\\tools\\real\"` — that ensures Windows file metadata is used during layer creation.
Ravi: Another note: the 403 on push might be a separate issue — if layer commit fails mid-upload, registry can respond 403 on finalize if the manifest refs a non-existent blob. If we re-tag and push a new digest it usually clears.
Melissa: Good point. For triage: 1) revert the symlink RUN in PR and push a patched image to unblock CI; 2) try a local build with `buildx build --platform windows/amd64 --load` on a Windows builder or on Linux with qemu/emulation if available; 3) if push still returns 403, try `docker manifest inspect` and `registry garbage-collect` conversation with registry infra if needed.
Alex: I'll revert the Dockerfile change now and push a fix. Can someone with Windows infra try building with `--platform=windows/amd64` and the PowerShell command to confirm?
Rohit: I can try in a bit on the Windows pool. Tag me. :thumbsup:
Jen: Also leaving a note for the author to include platform-aware steps in PR checklist.
Alex: Thanks — sending rollback in PR comment and opening a quick follow-up to rework link creation. :pray:
CI-Bot: rerun queued by Alex — job windows-build/win-latest (retry #3).
